newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia consumption tax seen replacing fuel tax.
newsitem.headline: Australia consumption tax seen replacing fuel tax.

text.p: Any new consumption tax in Australia should completely replace the excise on transport fuels for business, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade Tim Fischer told Australia's largest farm conference.
Addressing the New South Wales Farmers Association annual conference in Tamworth, Fischer said the Federal government remained committed to tax reform.

Arguments for the simple replacement of wholesale taxes by a consumption tax was not supported by the National Party, Fischer said. The National Party, which Fischer heads, is the Liberal Party's coalition partner in government.
"Our party made fuel tax the heart of tax reform when it said 'consumption tax in, transport fuel tax out'," Fischer said.
Fischer also reiterated the government's commitment to single desk monopoly marketing for wheat, sugar and rice.

"The single desk arrangements allow farmers to receive a premium they would not otherwise get, the nation gets a higher return on its exports and our customers can be assured of getting the product they seek," he said.

Fischer also told the conference of 500 delegates that draft Native Title legislation, which gives effect to the 10 point plan proposed by Australian Prime Minister John Howard, was not negotiable. He committed to continue consultations with interest groups until the end of July.
The bill is expected to be brought before parliament at the end of August or early September.
"The legislation reflects common law as determined by the High Court Wik decision (last year) but overcomes the uncertainty in relation to pastoral leases," he said.
